items.item_text: Current and valid California Clinical Laboratory Scientist License
Experience in transfusion medicine, blood separation processes, and quality control/quality assurance.
At least two years of recent experience performing testing in a clinical laboratory
Knowledge and experience with microbiology procedures
Experience with clinical trial processing and protocols

If you’re devoted to using your specialized clinical laboratory expertise to uncover the causes of diseases, you’ll find an exceptional home for your career at UCLA Health. Within our stimulating and supportive environment, you’ll collaborate with world-class clinicians while working with the latest in laboratory technology. If you’re looking to advance your career with one of the nation’s top health systems, we invite you to join us.
As a Clinical Laboratory Scientist of the Cell Therapy Lab, your job duties include:
Process/cryopreserve bone marrow and peripheral blood stem cells for infusion
Prepare samples for sterility, viability, and cell count testing
Operate blood separation instruments and hematology analyzer
Perform quality control tasks and computations
Document equipment maintenance and quality control
Maintain, troubleshoot, and perform minor repairs on lab equipment
Prepare written reports and technical summaries
Record/review data for accuracy, completeness, and suitability
Handle clinical trial administrative responsibilities
Follow and adapt to procedures/policies implemented by internal or External study sponsors on various clinical trials that may differ from standard operating procedures of BM/Stem cell laboratory.
Must adhere to all defined processing and documentation requirements for the clinical trial.
Must be able to work after-hours, weekends, and holidays when required (rotating on-call)
Recent demonstrated technical competence in cellular therapy product processing
Ability to use MS Office programs, including Word and Excel
Knowledge of hematologic malignancies, stem cell transplants, and cellular therapies
Skill in practical application of fractions, percentages, ratios, and proportions to be used in making reagents and in performing calculations
Ability to establish and maintain cooperative working relationships with outside services
Ability to work under conditions of frequent interruptions, distractions, and heavy workload while maintaining equanimity, accuracy and productivity
